b:
Two days
merging into the land of nature

A quiet train journey
through a forest with no one in it

The breeze that blew
played
many strange tricks

You could take
even that wind as a lover

As if God too had heard,
the view opened out
as the lovers leapt

The mother-laps
of tender tea leaves
plucked at a touch
brushed and made friends
with us as we squeezed past

The rubber estate
that welcomed us
to see us off
showed us a way
not even "Google" knew

The mountain waterfall
made us giddy;
perhaps because the giddiness of love
gathers there too,
it is the flower-lap
of lovers

The bus journey
took us
to a great lake,
and in between,
in the cold country,
a feast
of ice cream

A bicycle ride
at one with nature;
as the daughter of time grew dark
and the wind grew wild,
the way we ran
is a story of its own

To end our hunger
Annapoorani gave us
food to eat:
"Ambal's"

Reaching our lodging,
in a hut of our own,
a joyful party
for twins
not born of the same mother

The next day, once more,
a mountain waterfall;
no,
a waterfall from the sky:
she scattered by the handful
the streams of water
from the clouds

In the cool of the falls,
though leeches
clung to us,
though the stones
tested both our feet,
she gave us joy
without sorrow,
the beloved daughter
of the king of the sea

As Moon Plains,
our plains of dreams,
turned into a mirage,
we got
a "jet ski"

Showing off its speed,
pulling at the sky,
a wild ride
that flew
with screams

With the dream journey
stored as pictures in memory,
from now on,
with dreams
of God's own country,
we
note: The trip is to Sri Lanka's hill country; Moon Plains is a plateau near Nuwara Eliya. Annapoorani is the goddess of food; "Ambal's" is a restaurant. "God's own country" is the nickname of Kerala in India.
